stories.title: Salesforce Completes $3.6B Acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom), Folding It Into Agentforce
stories.body: Salesforce closed its $3.6 billion acquisition of Fin — the AI customer-service company formerly known as Intercom — on September 10, 2026, bringing more than 30,000 enterprise customers and Fin's autonomous agent platform into Agentforce. Fin's AI Agent claims to resolve 76% of support volume without human involvement across live chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, phone, and Slack, priced at $0.99 per resolved outcome. The deal folds Fin's proprietary Apex model and its engineering team into Salesforce AI Labs, with Fin continuing to operate as a standalone product inside the Salesforce stack.
stories.why: Any enterprise evaluating Fin or Intercom is now buying into the Salesforce platform lock-in story — a critical objection point and an opening to contrast Graas's independence and retail-data specialization. The $0.99/outcome pricing benchmark is now the market anchor; sellers need to be ready to defend or reframe outcome-based pricing conversations with retail and CPG procurement teams.

stories.title: Neo4j Launches Context Engine: A Shared Knowledge Layer With Business Ontology for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.body: Neo4j announced the Context Engine on October 20, 2026, positioning it as a reusable, shared knowledge substrate that lets AI agents consistently reason over enterprise data across systems. The product includes a predefined six-layer business ontology that maps organization, processes, data, and AI assets into a graph, plus a graph-native memory layer that logs agent reasoning and past decisions so agents learn over time. It also provides MCP-server integration for agent setup, connecting physical data sources directly to business logic at runtime.
stories.why: This is the clearest recent proof that the market has named 'context layer' as the missing piece before agents work reliably — directly validating the architecture Graas leads with on calls. Sellers can cite Neo4j's October launch as third-party confirmation that raw CRM or ERP data alone is insufficient and that a governed, ontology-grounded knowledge graph is the prerequisite infrastructure.

stories.title: Gartner & Forrester: 40%+ of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by 2027; 88% of Pilots Never Reach Production
stories.body: Gartner, polling more than 3,400 organizations, predicts over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027, attributing failures to escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate governance — not model capability. A separate September 2026 Gartner forecast adds that 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built by vendor forward-deployed engineering by 2028, citing rising maintenance costs and outside-engineer dependence. Forrester's 2026 report, titled 'Companies Are Chasing, Few Are Catching,' found roughly three-quarters of enterprise leaders claiming to adopt agentic AI but only a fraction running it in real production, with 88% of pilots (per a Forrester/Anaconda study) never reaching production due to missing evaluation criteria and governance friction.
stories.why: This analyst consensus is the sharpest objection-handler available: when a prospect says 'we're already running pilots,' sellers can cite these numbers to shift the conversation to what it takes to get from pilot to production — which is exactly the data-foundation and governance layer Graas provides. The Gartner September 2026 'vendor forward-deployed engineering' forecast also directly challenges build-with-a-consultancy approaches.

stories.title: McKinsey Agentic Commerce Consumer Survey (Oct 2026): AI Search Now 3x More Influential Than Traditional Search for Retail Decisions
stories.body: McKinsey's Agentic Commerce Consumer Survey, fielded in June 2026 across approximately 21,000 consumers in 11 markets, finds that for AI users, AI search is three times more influential than traditional search in purchase decisions. The report notes that agentic commerce is helping e-commerce laggards close competitive gaps rapidly, and flags that implementation complications led OpenAI to scale back its instant-checkout ambitions — a signal that the agent execution layer remains harder than it looks. Forrester's mid-2026 assessment, cited in the same research ecosystem, states bluntly that most 'agentic' commerce experiences today are still conversational, with humans still driving checkout in the vast majority of cases.
stories.why: A McKinsey survey with 21,000 respondents published October 28, 2026 is the strongest external proof point that enterprise retailers must act now on agentic commerce infrastructure — not in 2027. The finding that even well-resourced players like OpenAI have stumbled on execution reinforces why a pre-built, retail-specific context layer matters more than a DIY agent build.

stories.tag: US - named CPG deployment with outcomes
stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI Boosts In-Stocks by 2–4% and Planning Productivity by 60%+ in CPG–Retailer Supply Chain Pilots
stories.body: BCG's published analysis of large CPG and retailer deployments finds that agentic AI unlocks 2–4 percentage points of in-stock improvement and more than 60% planning productivity gains by enabling synchronized replenishment — agents monitor store- and DC-level inventory signals against sell-through velocity and proactively push replenishment recommendations before a retailer's own cycle catches a pending stockout. A separate named case from analytics firm Tredence shows an enterprise CPG client's deduction-management agent, integrated across 30-plus systems including SAP and EDI portals, recovered $6.5 million from roughly $40 million in addressable trade deduction spend. Both deployments cite the same prerequisite: a unified, real-time data layer spanning retailer feeds, ERP, and demand signals.
stories.why: These are named outcome numbers — in-stock rates and recovered revenue — that a Graas seller can put on a slide for a supply-chain or category-management conversation with a CPG or distributor prospect. Both cases explicitly name data harmonization as the prerequisite, making them direct proof that the context/data foundation layer is not optional overhead but the source of the measurable return.
